key_insight: A stable Galerkin reduced-order model combined with an extended Kalman filter can accurately estimate the full Rayleigh-Bénard convection state from sparse velocity data alone.
engineering_relevance: This enables lower-cost sensing and real-time monitoring of thermal-fluid systems, with implications for flow control, experimental diagnostics, and reduced instrumentation design.
method: Build a stable ROM from controllability modes of the linearised Boussinesq equations.
Use the ROM as the EKF prediction model and DNS-generated synthetic measurements for assimilation.
Apply the Kalman gain to rank sensors and prune the least informative ones greedily.
evidence_signal: Across periodic, quasiperiodic, and chaotic regimes, the filter tracks energetic modes well and achieves time-averaged reconstruction errors below 14% for velocity and 9% for temperature.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and regime validity of the ROM, so coarse or strongly off-model measurements may reduce EKF robustness.
paper_title: State estimation of Rayleigh-Bénard convection with reduced-order models
